claim: P1 engineering non-inferiority of three frozen consumer-shaped scheduling replays against Marl under the same four-worker physical-core contract

configuration.delivery_shape: source-built static library in a separate peer process
configuration.scheduler: Marl owns worker scheduling, fibers, Event/ConditionVariable, WaitGroup and channel synchronization composition
configuration.cancellation: C++23 std::stop_token from the same MSVC 19.50 toolchain supplies the O(1) poll because Marl has no cancellation-token product primitive
configuration.caller_participation: disabled; both sides use four dedicated workers and one external submitting/completion caller

ownership_topology.candidate: One external caller submits preallocated raw callbacks; HYLE workers poll one shared CancelToken, process one short tile, publish to one bounded HYLE Channel and signal a WaitGroup
ownership_topology.peer: The same caller and preallocated records enqueue Marl tasks; Marl workers poll one shared standard stop_token, process the identical tile, publish to an equal-capacity Marl mutex/ConditionVariable ring and signal Marl WaitGroup
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both processes retain four dedicated pinned workers, 16384 admitted callbacks, identical input and tile code, one non-cancelled O(1) poll, equal bounded capacity, exact result collection and persistent scheduler lifetime

material_contribution.derivation: The sched-v1 closure card admits short CPU callbacks with external injection, cancellation and bounded producer/consumer collection as a normal foundation journey

workloads.semantic_contract: Dispatch, cancellation-poll, compute, publish, complete and collect every admitted short request without loss or hidden caller execution

input.distribution: fixed deterministic uint64 input with per-callback seed

workloads.setup: Scheduler/thread creation, exact CPU pinning, input/context/channel/token construction, expected checksum and a 2048-callback warmup are outside the measured interval
charged_phases: WaitGroup completion and exact result drain

pair.candidate: HYLE raw schedule + CancelToken + Channel + WaitGroup
pair.peer: Marl Task + std::stop_token + Marl synchronization channel composition + WaitGroup

ownership_topology.candidate: One admitted root fiber creates 128 single-cell non-suspending schedule_task<uint64_t> values per batch, retains JoinHandles, waits through dynamic when_all, consumes typed results and completes every callable/result-cell lifecycle
ownership_topology.peer: One admitted Marl root fiber enqueues 128 Marl tasks per batch, retains preallocated typed result slots, waits through Marl WaitGroup and consumes every result
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both root fibers run 16 batches on four dedicated pinned workers, use identical input/tile/seed/result accounting, exclude root admission and persistent scheduler setup and include full per-task ownership plus batch join lifecycle

material_contribution.derivation: Current Graph source consumes dynamic typed spawn/join from a scheduler fiber and fixes 1024 elements as its automatic grain floor; this is a consumer boundary rather than a benchmark-only noop

workloads.semantic_contract: Fan out typed nonzero tile tasks, wait for each complete dynamic batch and consume every exact result with no detached lifetime

input.distribution: fixed deterministic 1024-element uint64 tile with per-task seed

workloads.setup: Scheduler/thread creation, exact CPU pinning, input allocation, expected checksum, vector reservation, root admission and a 64-task warmup are outside the measured interval
charged_phases: typed result collection and callable/cell lifecycle teardown

ownership_topology.candidate: One persistent pinned HYLE fiber per worker publishes a fresh episode Waker, suspends, is woken from the external caller and acknowledges resume before the next episode
ownership_topology.peer: One persistent pinned Marl fiber per worker publishes episode readiness, waits on an auto-reset Marl Event, is signalled from the same external-caller role and acknowledges resume
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both processes exclude scheduler/fiber setup and 256 warmups, retain four persistent pinned fibers, perform 4096 four-way completion episodes, block the external role while awaiting acknowledgements and charge publication, cross-thread wake, reinjection/unpark, resume and acknowledgement

material_contribution.derivation: Current IO and GPU polling sources converge on the sched Waker completion spine; persistent episodes avoid contaminating the result with fiber construction

workloads.semantic_contract: Wake and resume exactly one already-owned suspended fiber on every pinned worker for every external completion episode without lost wakeups or migration
workloads.setup: Scheduler/thread creation, exact CPU pinning, persistent fiber admission and 256 complete wake episodes are outside the measured interval
